title: GS21 product economy (gvyp10) with a rare priced CRASH in the state y: a different distribution of shocks
question: Does a priced second factor make a fair gap in GS21 when the exposure is the PRODUCT of two within-firm states that two different characteristics reveal, so the premium is bilinear in the ranks?
notes:
GROUP 1 (different distributions: crash) in GS21, which had no run in that cell (the default channel is dormant and disasters were declined). gvyp10's economy with the y chain's transition replaced by a mixture: with probability gs_pj 0.01 a month the state jumps to its lowest node (-2.5 sd) instead of following the Tauchen transition, and the jump is priced by its own kernel factor exp(gs_gj) with gs_gj 2.0 (a risk-neutral jump probability of 7.4% a month before renormalisation), not by the Gaussian price extrapolated to a ten-sd move. The firms' exposure to the crash is the same product structure as to the diffusive state.

PRE-CHECK (low resolution, 2026-10-12): ranks R2 0.55 / products 0.91 / market 54% / cs-sd 3.3 %/yr, SR_max 0.38 against gvyp10's 0.48 / 0.90 / 51% / 4.6 / 0.44: the crash lowers the attainable Sharpe a little and leaves the premium's shape. gs_pj 0.02 and gs_gj 1.1 give the same picture.

PRECOMMITMENT STATUS: precommitted=false; id read from the Quest solve log before any seed runs. Mechanism probe.

PREDICTION (2026-10-12, before the run): the crash changes the level of premia, not their shape: room and fair gap within noise of gvyp10's (+0.194, +0.0196). FALSIFIED as 'the distribution of shocks matters for the gap' if the fair gap differs from gvyp10's by more than +-0.010 on the same seeds in 7 of 10.

changes: gs_bv [0.1] x gs_bzb 1.0 z~ b~: productivity x coupon exposure, single type
the y factor moves the COST, exp(gs_bc y), with types gs_bc [0.0]; production exposure gs_bv 0, no level compensation (at y = 0 every type pays the same cost)
everything else gvy25's: 9-node priced y chain, gamma_v 2.5, kappa_y 0.35

method.gs_vy_exposure: production x exp(gs_bv gs_bzb z~ b~ y)

seeds.policy: run_oracle.py --seed drives BOTH the firm-level shocks and the aggregate y path (reg_seed offset by the seed).
